      "exact_statement": "The following results are used from the classification and representation theory of finite simple groups.*\n\n1.  *A maximal subgroup of an almost simple classical group, not containing its socle, is a stabilizer in one of Aschbacher’s eight geometric collections, or has an almost simple irreducible component. The geometric collections are subspace or flag stabilizers, direct-sum decompositions, extension-field structures, tensor products, subfield structures, symplectic-type groups, tensor-induced decompositions, and forms. Graph automorphisms may interchange the relevant subspaces or flag members; triality and exceptional graph–field automorphisms occur only in bounded rank. We use (Aschbacher 1984) [[Aschbacher1984](#ref-Aschbacher1984)] and the almost simple formulation and descriptions in (Kleidman and Liebeck 1990, Table 1.2.A and Theorem 1.2.1, pp. 3–4) [[KleidmanLiebeck1990](#ref-KleidmanLiebeck1990)], with the geometric descriptions in Chapters 3–5; the connected tensor structures and their finite fixed-point versions are also given in (Liebeck and Seitz 1998, Theorem 2 and Section 4(5)) [[LiebeckSeitzClassical1998](#ref-LiebeckSeitzClassical1998)].*\n\n2.  *The maximal subgroups of alternating and symmetric groups have the intransitive, imprimitive, affine, diagonal, product-action, or almost simple alternatives of the maximal-subgroup form of the O’Nan–Scott Theorem. The relevant formulation and all the alternatives used here are recorded in the proof of (Burness, Liebeck, and Shalev 2017, Proposition 3.1) [[BurnessLiebeckShalev2017](#ref-BurnessLiebeckShalev2017)].*\n\n3.  *For a fixed algebraic type, sufficiently general finite subgroups lie between the derived group and the inner-diagonal group of a finite fixed-point group. The complementary alternative is containment in a proper algebraic subgroup of bounded complexity. The bounded-envelope version permits passage to the reductive simple quotients of that subgroup; see (Larsen and Pink 2011, Theorems 0.5 and 12.3) [[LarsenPink2011](#ref-LarsenPink2011)].*\n\n4.  *A subgroup maximal in a maximal subgroup of an almost simple group has at most five nonabelian chief factors (Burness, Liebeck, and Shalev 2017, Proposition 8.1) [[BurnessLiebeckShalev2017](#ref-BurnessLiebeckShalev2017)]. The number refers to chief factors, not to their simple direct factors.*\n\n5.  *If $[H,A]$ is a height-two interval and $A$ is alternating or symmetric of degree at least five, it has at most eleven interior vertices (Basile 2001, Theorem D) [[Basile2008](#ref-Basile2008)]. Here the entire interval is required to have height two: $H$ is maximal in every maximal overgroup. This is the hypothesis imposed whenever the result is used.*\n\n6.  *Cross-characteristic irreducible projective degrees satisfy the Landazuri–Seitz lower bounds (Landazuri and Seitz 1974) [[LandazuriSeitz1974](#ref-LandazuriSeitz1974)]. In particular, outside bounded rank, a source of natural dimension $n$ and field parameter $q$ requires degree at least $q^{c n}$ for an absolute $c>0$; the applicable classical bounds are recorded in (Häsä 2014, Tables 3–6) [[Hasa2014](#ref-Hasa2014)]. Above an absolute classical rank, every perfect central cover of a finite simple classical group is a central quotient of its usual simply connected fixed-point group, uniformly over all finite fields, including the standard graph twists (Steinberg 1981, Theorem 1.1 and p. 528) [[Steinberg1981](#ref-Steinberg1981)]. The central-cover deduction and preservation of representations are proved in Lemma <a href=\"#lift:finite-covers\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lift:finite-covers\">44</a>.         "exact_quote": "In the initial projection, consider chain vertices strictly above the original starting vertex $a$, and write $$K_i=H_*P_i,\\qquad C_i=\\operatorname{core}_{K_i}(H_*),\n \\qquad Q_i=C_i\\cap P_i,$$ and let $R_i/Q_i$ be its active nonabelian chief factor.         "exact_quote": "Fix a connected adjoint simple algebraic type $\\Phi$. There is a constant $c_\\Phi$ such that a finite subgroup $P$ of an algebraic group $X$ of type $\\Phi$ has one of the following descriptions.*\n\n1.  *For a Frobenius map $F_0$, $$E=(X^{F_0})'\\leq P\\leq X^{F_0},$$ where $E$ is simple.*\n\n2.  *Every nonabelian composition factor of $P$ of order greater than $c_\\Phi$ is of Lie type in the characteristic of $X$, with algebraic dimension strictly less than $\\dim X$. The total number of nonabelian composition factors, counted with multiplicity, is at most $c_\\Phi$.*\n\n*In particular, the ranks of nonabelian simple sections of finite groups of Lie type of rank at most $R$ are bounded by a function of $R$; simple sections of bounded order are included in this bound.",

          "anchor": "stmt-cls-envelopes",
          "exact_quote": "Fix a connected adjoint simple algebraic type $\\Phi$. There is a constant $c_\\Phi$ such that a finite subgroup $P$ of an algebraic group $X$ of type $\\Phi$ has one of the following descriptions.*\n\n1.  *For a Frobenius map $F_0$, $$E=(X^{F_0})'\\leq P\\leq X^{F_0},$$ where $E$ is simple.*\n\n2.  *Every nonabelian composition factor of $P$ of order greater than $c_\\Phi$ is of Lie type in the characteristic of $X$, with algebraic dimension strictly less than $\\dim X$. The total number of nonabelian composition factors, counted with multiplicity, is at most $c_\\Phi$.*\n\n*In particular, the ranks of nonabelian simple sections of finite groups of Lie type of rank at most $R$ are bounded by a function of $R$; simple sections of bounded order are included in this bound.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }

        "anchor": "stmt-cls-reduction",
        "exact_quote": "If Theorem <a href=\"#cls:chain-rigidity\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"cls:chain-rigidity\">14</a> is false, then for every $s$ and $R$ there is a retained chain of at least $s$ vertices, with all its original two-edge shortcuts and normal-group tests, such that:*\n\n1.  *all endpoint types are distinct classical types; their ranks, and the ranks of all shortcut middle types, exceed $R$;*\n\n2.  *all endpoint multiplicities are equal. Thus each comparison, projected to one upper active coordinate, has one active simple factor;*\n\n3.  *the killed kernels of all endpoint and shortcut comparisons are soluble. Every endpoint inner comparison has exactly its one active simple factor as a nonabelian composition factor;*\n\n4.  *there is a pool of absolutely bounded cardinality containing all nonabelian simple types in every projected active-factor and fiber stabilizer in the fixed $H_*$, and in their induced images, used in these comparisons. No assertion concerns the entire unprojected original stabilizers. The splitting multiplicities and invariant-block indices have boundedly many possible values;*\n\n5.  *each shortcut is either two strict steps, both with one active simple factor and all other inner composition factors soluble, or a strict split followed downwards by an equal-type merge. The latter is geometric. In geometric steps the inactive dimensions have boundedly many possible values once their simple labels and bounded structural choices are fixed; when all inactive components are soluble these dimensions are absolutely bounded.*\n\n*All bounds described as absolute are uniform over the original groups. This proposition introduces no new lattice tests at the retained bottom.",

      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-cls-cat-cross",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"cls:catalogue\" label=\"cls:catalogue\"></span> Consider a strict labelled cover and its one-coordinate maximal subgroup $M$ in an almost simple group with socle $T$, as supplied by Proposition <a href=\"#frm:projection\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"frm:projection\">10</a>. Mark its active nonabelian chief factor. The non-geometric irreducible category below means that its simple source acts absolutely irreducibly on the ambient natural module and that the maximal subgroup is outside all geometric collections, in particular the subfield collection. All growing-rank assertions refer to growing *source* rank. There are absolute constants $C,c>0$ with the following properties.*\n\n\n\n1.  *<span id=\"cls:cat-geometric\" label=\"cls:cat-geometric\"></span> For unbounded-rank classical active types, a geometric defining-characteristic step changes natural dimension by taking a subspace or quotient, a repeated natural module, a tensor product, or restriction of scalars. Subfield steps leave natural dimension unchanged and multiply the field exponent by a prime. An extension-field step, read upwards from the active factor, has $$\\label{grw:matrix-field-convention}\n     n_t=b n_s,\\qquad\n     \\epsilon_s f_s=b\\epsilon_t f_t,\n     \\qquad f_t=\\frac{\\epsilon_s}{b\\epsilon_t}f_s,$$ where $b$ is the prime degree between natural matrix fields. A twisted-tensor step has $$\\label{grw:twisted-field-convention}\n     n_t=n_s^b,\\qquad f_s=b f_t,$$ exactly; here $b$ is prime, after bounded source-rank cases are removed. All other changes of field exponent belong to a fixed finite set of positive rational factors.*\n\n2.  *<span id=\"cls:cat-inactive\" label=\"cls:cat-inactive\"></span> If there is one active simple component and the other geometric components are soluble, their natural dimensions are absolutely bounded. The active dimension in a subspace case is comparable with the ambient dimension; a totally singular summand and its dual may represent the same active component twice. A nontrivial parabolic radical in these cases has order between $q^{c n_t}$ and $q^{C n_t^2}$. For a fixed ambient group, once the active slot, other component dimensions, and the bounded flag/form choices are fixed, there are boundedly many possible orders of the full inner stabilizer divided by the order of its active simple factor, with multiplicity included.*\n\n3.  *<span id=\"cls:cat-symplectic\" label=\"cls:cat-symplectic\"></span> A symplectic-type step of unbounded active rank is cross-characteristic. Its source is symplectic or orthogonal over a prime field of order $r$, of natural dimension $2d+O(1)$, and its target natural dimension is $n_t=r^d$. If $P=M\\cap T$, then $$c n_t^2\\leq |P|/|T_s|\\leq C n_t^2.$$ Its target field exponent is at most $|T_s|^C$.*\n\n4.  *<span id=\"cls:cat-nonlinear\" label=\"cls:cat-nonlinear\"></span> After the twisted-tensor case in <a href=\"#cls:cat-geometric\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"cls:cat-geometric\">[cls:cat-geometric]</a> is separated off, a defining-characteristic almost simple irreducible step has a single nonzero restricted, nonnatural Frobenius digit, up to a common Frobenius twist. This restricted module may have further tensor factors in a very special characteristic. Its dimension is at least $c n_s^2$. Its source and target field exponents differ by a rational factor from a fixed finite set. Natural, dual-natural, and natural-size special-isogeny representations are included among the geometric cases instead.*\n\n5.  *For a cross-characteristic almost simple step, $$q_s^{c n_s}\\leq n_t\\leq |T_s|^C,\n     \\qquad f_t\\leq |T_s|^C.$$ The upper degree bound also holds in defining characteristic. For this and the preceding irreducible case, the homomorphism from the ambient automorphism normalizer of the source simple group to its automorphism group has kernel of absolute bounded order. In particular, a subgroup of that normalizer has order at most $C$ times the order of its induced automorphism group of the source.",
        "source_id": "PM-206.2"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {

All growing-rank assertions refer to growing *source* rank.         "anchor": "stmt-grw-remaining-paths",
        "exact_quote": "If the reduced chains of Proposition <a href=\"#cls:reduction\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"cls:reduction\">25</a> have arbitrary length, then they still have arbitrary length subject to all of the following properties.*\n\n1.  *The endpoints have a common classical family and field $q=p^f$, their natural dimensions tend to infinity, and their common factor multiplicity is $m$. Every selected shortcut has one active factor at each cover and no other nonabelian factor in its inner projection.*\n\n2.  *Every selected two-edge shortcut contains a defining-characteristic nonlinear cover. Its representation is a single Frobenius digit after the twisted-tensor geometric alternative has been separated. The other cover is another such nonlinear cover, or a block, form, tensor, extension-field, subfield, or twisted-tensor cover. No crossing, symplectic-type cover, or parabolic cover with a large unipotent radical remains. The characteristic-two nonsingular-line form inclusion is retained, with its natural simple quotient convention.*\n\n3.  *There are fixed constants $b,C$ and a fixed finite set $\\mathcal R\\subset\\mathbb Q_{>0}$ such that every intermediate exponent satisfies $f'/f\\in\\mathcal R$, every field-extension or twisted-tensor degree is at most $b$, and every inactive geometric natural dimension is at most $b$.         "anchor": "stmt-lift-finite-covers",
        "exact_quote": "There is an absolute rank bound, independent of the finite field, with the following property. Let $\\mathbf G$ be a simply connected classical algebraic group above this bound, let $\\sigma$ be a standard split or graph-twisted Steinberg map, and put $U=\\mathbf G^\\sigma$. Then $U$ is perfect, $H_2(U,\\mathbb Z)=0$, and its standard simple quotient map $u:U\\twoheadrightarrow S$ is central. For any quasisimple central extension $a:L\\twoheadrightarrow S$, there is a unique homomorphism $\\pi:U\\to L$ satisfying $a\\pi=u$. It is surjective and has central kernel. A specified projective representation of $L$ also lifts uniquely to a linear representation of $U$ over an algebraically closed field.",
        "source_id": "PM-206.2"

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lift-nonsingular-line",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(W,Q)$ be a nonsingular quadratic space of even dimension $2r+2$ over $\\mathbb F_q$, where $r\\geq3$ and $q$ is even, and let $v\\in W$ satisfy $Q(v)\\neq0$. Write $B$ for the polar form and $\\overline W=v^\\perp/\\langle\nv\\rangle$. The kernel of $$O(W,Q)_{\\langle v\\rangle}\\longrightarrow\n \\operatorname{Sp}(\\overline W,B)$$ is the central group generated by the symmetry $$r_v(x)=x+\\frac{B(x,v)}{Q(v)}v.$$ The image is the full symplectic group.         "exact_quote": "In the setting of Proposition <a href=\"#grw:remaining-paths\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"grw:remaining-paths\">41</a>, each retained projected subgroup $P$ has a characteristic normal quasisimple subgroup $L=P^{(\\infty)}$ and $P/L$ is soluble. In a fixed higher coordinate, these components nest with the projected subgroups and are normalized by their common bottom action. All intermediate components of a shortcut are normalized by its lower coordinate stabilizer.         "anchor": "stmt-ext-e4",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"ext:reduction\" label=\"ext:reduction\"></span> If either orientation of the decorated lattice has a finite-group interval representation, there are finite groups $A\\le D$, finite nonabelian simple groups $T,R$, a homomorphism $\\alpha:A\\to\\operatorname{Aut}(T)$, and extensions $$\\beta_J:U_J\\to\\operatorname{Aut}(T)\n       \\qquad(\\varnothing\\ne J\\subsetneq\\{1,\\ldots,4\\})$$ with the following properties. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Fenced bounded lattice interval** ([source](#stmt-auto-definition-1)): A bounded lattice interval $[a,b]$ is *fenced* if it has an interior element and, for each $a<c<b$, there are $a<u<v<b$ such that $$c\wedge u=c\wedge v=a, \qquad c\vee u=c\vee v=b.$$
- **Bottom core and labelled socle** ([source](#stmt-frm-labels)): Suppose that $[D,X]$ is fenced, and put $$F_X=\operatorname{core}_X(D) =\bigcap_{g\in X}D^g.$$ Then $X/F_X$ has a unique minimal normal subgroup $$\label{frm:socle-label} S_X=N_X/F_X\cong T_X^{m_X},$$ where $T_X$ is nonabelian simple and $N_X$ is its full inverse image in $X$. Moreover, $$X=DN_X.$$ Every nontrivial normal subgroup of $X/F_X$ contains $S_X$, and $$C_{X/F_X}(S_X)=1.$$ In particular, $X/F_X$ has no nontrivial soluble normal subgroup. If $I_X$ is the set of simple direct factors of $S_X$, then $D$ and $X$ induce the same transitive permutation group on $I_X$.
- **Subdirect subgroup** ([source](#pm-h-8)): For a direct product $T^I=\prod_{i\in I}T_i$, with each $T_i\cong T$, a subgroup is *subdirect* if all coordinate projections are surjective.
- **Full diagonal strip** ([source](#pm-h-8)): A *full diagonal strip* on a nonempty subset $J\subseteq I$ is a subgroup obtained by identifying all the $T_j$, $j\in J$, by isomorphisms, and putting identity elements outside $J$.
- **Saturation relative to an upper vertex** ([source](#pm-h-9)): Call $D\le Z\le Y$ *saturated relative to $Y$* if $(Z\cap N_Y)/F_Y$ is the product of its coordinate projections.
- **Tested chain** ([source](#stmt-cls-test-normal)): Let $D<a<b$ belong to a finite group interval, and let $$a=x_0<x_1<\cdots <x_N=b.$$ A tested chain consists of these vertices and vertices $v_{ij}$ for $0\leq i<j\leq N$, with the following properties. 1. Every $x_i$ and $v_{ij}$ is labelled: its interval above $D$ is fenced. Moreover, $x_i\prec v_{ij}\prec x_j$, where both relations are covers in the entire interval. 2. Every $[x_i,x_j]$, $i<j$, is fenced. 3. Every $x_i$ with $i<N$, and every $v_{ij}$ with $j<N$, is an intersection of coatoms of $[a,b]$. The $v_{iN}$ are coatoms by <a href="#cls:test-labels" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cls:test-labels">[cls:test-labels]</a>. 4. Put $$\mathcal U=\{x_j:1\leq j\leq N\} \mathbin{\cup}\{v_{ij}:1\leq i<j\leq N\}.$$ For each $u\in\mathcal U$, the interval $[a,u]$ is fenced, $a$ is an intersection of its coatoms, and there is $a<c_u<u$ such that the *entire* interval $[c_u,u]$ is $M_{16}$. 5. For $i<j$ and $x_i\leq z\leq x_j$, either $[D,z]$ is fenced, or there is a labelled $z'$ with $x_i\leq z'<z$ which is comparable with every vertex of $[D,z]$. No additional requirement is imposed on $[a,v_{0j}]$. In particular, <a href="#cls:test-alternating" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cls:test-alternating">[cls:test-alternating]</a> never subdivides the cover $a\prec v_{0j}$.
- **Action levels** ([source](#pm-h-12)): We call the induced coset actions of $K_{j-1}$ on $K_{j-1}/K_j$ its *action levels*.
- **Nonabelian composition-factor type set** ([source](#pm-h-13)): For a finite group $H$, write $\operatorname{cf}_{\mathrm{na}}(H)$ for its set of nonabelian simple composition-factor types.
- **Quasisimple group** ([source](#lift:section)): A group is *quasisimple* if it is perfect and its quotient by its centre is nonabelian simple.
- **Terminal derived subgroup** ([source](#lift:section)): We write $P^{(\infty)}$ for the terminal member of the derived series of a finite group $P$.
- **Frobenius twist** ([source](#pm-h-28)): Here and below a Frobenius twist $M^{[a]}$ means pullback by the $p^a$-power Frobenius morphism.
- **Natural-type simple module** ([source](#pm-h-36)): We call a nontrivial simple module *of natural type* if it is a Frobenius twist of a natural simple module or its dual, allowing the central, diagram, and characteristic-two $B/C$ isogenies in the chosen realization.
- **Private insertion** ([source](#pm-h-43)): A *private insertion of $Q$ into $[a,b]$* retains the old orders and introduces no comparisons between an old vertex and a fresh interior vertex except those forced through $a$ and $b$.
- **Fencing insertion** ([source](#pm-h-43)): A *fencing insertion* means two separate chain insertions, each with exactly two fresh interior vertices, into the same interval.
- **Insertion batch** ([source](#pm-h-43)): This means a finite list of private insertions all of whose endpoints were present before the batch.
- **Invariant subdirect extension pair** ([source](#stmt-ext-dictionary)): Let a finite group $D$ act on $S=\prod_{i\in I}T_i$, where all $T_i$ are isomorphic to a nonabelian simple group $T$, and suppose that its action on $I$ is transitive. Fix $i_0\in I$, set $A=D_{i_0}$, identify $T_{i_0}$ with $T$, and let $\alpha:A\to\operatorname{Aut}(T)$ be the induced action.* *The $D$-invariant subdirect subgroups of $S$ are in bijection with pairs $(U,\beta)$, where $$A\le U\le D,\qquad \beta:U\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(T),\qquad \beta\|_A=\alpha.$$ Write $S(U,\beta)$ for the corresponding subgroup. Then $$\label{ext:dictionary-order} S(U,\beta)\le S(V,\gamma) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad V\le U\ \hbox{ and }\ \beta\|_V=\gamma.$$ In particular, the interval of $D$-invariant subgroups from $S(U,\beta)$ to $S$ is anti-isomorphic to $[A,U]$, by restricting $\beta$.
- **Support preimage** ([source](#pm-h-53)): For $B\subseteq I_J$, let $$\label{glue:support-preimage} N_J(B)=q_J^{-1}\left(\prod_{i\in B}S_{J,i}\right), \qquad q_J:N_J\longrightarrow S_J=N_J/C_J,$$ where $S_{J,i}$ are the simple direct factors of $S_J$.

## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-normal-test** [claim](#stmt-frm-normal-test) / [proof](#proof-stmt-frm-normal-test): Apply the subgroup modular identity to comparable complements and then pass to inverse images in the quotient. -> Normal-subgroup dichotomy and nonmodularity.
- **step-socle-labels** [claim](#stmt-frm-labels) / [proof](#proof-stmt-frm-labels): Factor out the bottom core; exclude abelian and competing minimal normal subgroups using the fence. -> Unique nonabelian socle label and full factor action.
- **step-bottlenecks** [claim](#stmt-frm-bottleneck) / [proof](#proof-stmt-frm-bottleneck): Use comparability at the bottleneck and the nonabelian labelled socle. -> Soluble-normal and commuting-normal tests above a bottleneck.
- **step-subdirect-strips** [claim](#stmt-frm-subdirect) / [proof](#proof-stmt-frm-subdirect): Induct on coordinates and analyze projection kernels onto a nonabelian simple factor. -> Canonical diagonal-strip partition and refinement rule.
- **step-equal-transport** [claim](#stmt-frm-equal-transport) / [proof](#proof-stmt-frm-equal-transport): Compare simple sections, use bottom transitivity, and identify subdirect strips with the lower socle. -> Equal-type equivalence and composable equivariant support maps.
- **step-strict-products** [claim](#stmt-frm-strict-product) / [proof](#proof-stmt-frm-strict-product): Compare the coordinate product closure with comparable fence complements or coatom maximality. -> Saturation and saturation of coatom intersections.
- **step-coordinate-projection** [claim](#stmt-frm-projection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-frm-projection): Intersect coatom constraints to identify the inner bottom, then lift all coordinate overgroups. -> Entire almost simple coordinate interval preserving covers.
- **step-active-transport** [claim](#stmt-frm-active-transport) / [proof](#proof-stmt-frm-active-transport): Split original cores and perfect socle preimages into products and compare actual projected cores. -> Active chief factors, multiplicities, and full local factor actions.
- **step-classification-inputs** [claim](#stmt-cls-literature) / [proof](#stmt-cls-literature): Retain the cited classification and representation inputs with their individual hypotheses. -> Literature inputs for the uniform reductions.
- **step-factor-action-levels** [claim](#stmt-cls-cat-actions) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-cat-actions): Inspect full component and block actions in the maximal-subgroup alternatives. -> Bounded-depth small or natural giant action levels.
- **step-bounded-routes** [claim](#stmt-cls-routes) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-routes): Induct through action kernels and retain large alternating supports in arbitrary overgroups. -> Uniform height, index-count, and nonabelian-type bounds.
- **step-common-index-palette** [claim](#stmt-cls-index-recipes) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-index-recipes): Express indices using common rational atoms and explicitly control denominator routes. -> Bounded union of index recipes across all permitted operations.
- **step-uniform-active-actions** [claim](#stmt-cls-uniform-actions) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-uniform-actions): Use original shortcuts and full local actions to build common projected type and index pools. -> Bounded equal-type stretches and common multiplicity-ratio palette.
- **step-core-gaps** [claim](#stmt-cls-core-gaps) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-core-gaps): Embed killed kernels in descending projected-core gaps and retain a soluble stretch. -> Soluble killed kernels and one-factor endpoint inner comparisons.
- **step-alternating-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-cls-alternating) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-alternating): Project the entire tested height-two interval and compare it with the alternating interval bound. -> Exclusion of large alternating upper types.
- **step-bounded-envelopes** [claim](#stmt-cls-envelopes) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-envelopes): Apply fixed-type envelopes and analyze their reductive simple quotients and component groups. -> Smaller-dimensional factor alternative and bounded ranks of sections.
- **step-normalized-subfields** [claim](#stmt-cls-subfields) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-subfields): Compute the pointwise isogeny centralizer and force a prime Frobenius power by maximality. -> Normalized prime subfield step and intermediate fixed-point groups.
- **step-bounded-rank-chains** [claim](#stmt-cls-bounded-rank) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-bounded-rank): Thin to fixed family and dimension, then compare prime counts through original shortcuts. -> Bounded bounded-rank type count and large-rank retained middles.
- **step-classical-reduction** [claim](#stmt-cls-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-reduction): Remove equal-type stretches, exclude alternating and bounded-rank types, and use Ramsey on multiplicity ratios. -> Distinct large-rank classical endpoints with equal multiplicities and controlled shortcut alternatives.
- **step-irreducible-normalizers** [claim](#stmt-cls-normalizer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-normalizer): Use Schur centralizers and minimal-field descent for the whole normalizer outside the subfield collection. -> Absolute normalizer-kernel bound and classical outer-order bound.
- **step-standard-covers** [claim](#stmt-lift-finite-covers) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lift-finite-covers): Discard bounded-rank multiplier exceptions and split central extensions using vanishing integral homology. -> Unique finite central-cover maps and unique linear projective lifts.
- **step-twisted-tensor-maximality** [claim](#stmt-cls-twisted-tensor) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-twisted-tensor): Preserve the intrinsic digit tensor algebras, replace them by full classical factors, and exclude a composite cycle by grouped tensor structures. -> Geometric twisted-tensor step with prime cycle and exact usual-field relation.
- **step-maximal-step-estimates** [claim](#stmt-cls-cat-cross) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cls-cat-cross): Read full geometric stabilizers and combine degree classifications, minimal-field bounds, and irreducible normalizers. -> Field, dimension, order, and normalizer estimates by cover category.
- **step-stabilizer-transport** [claim](#stmt-grw-input-normalizers) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-input-normalizers): Identify actual factor stabilizers through the equal-multiplicity support bijection and use conjugation on the intermediate source. -> Bound on the actual lower upper-coordinate stabilizer.
- **step-prime-colors** [claim](#stmt-grw-prime-colors) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-prime-colors): Color by bounded valuation vectors and total unsigned complexity outside a fixed prime set. -> Constant homogeneous triangles and long constant subarrays.
- **step-opposite-field-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-grw-opposite-fields) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-opposite-fields): Apply prime-complexity coloring to exact dimension ratios or logarithmic dimension ratios. -> No arbitrarily long homogeneous opposite-field configuration.
- **step-geometric-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-grw-no-geometric) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-no-geometric): Equalize fields and families, then bound the number of geometric outputs from a fixed lower endpoint. -> No arbitrary-length purely geometric shortcut chain.
- **step-inner-quotient-multiplication** [claim](#stmt-grw-indices) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-indices): Multiply actual group indices under saturation and take the positive common-multiplicity root. -> Positive integral inner quotients multiplying through endpoints and shortcuts.
- **step-coordinate-normal-tests** [claim](#stmt-grw-normal-commuting) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-normal-commuting): Apply original fences or labelled bottlenecks modulo the higher original core in the same actual proper enlargement. -> Killed soluble products and the commuting-normal alternative.
- **step-small-stabilizer-parabolic** [claim](#stmt-grw-small-parabolic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-small-parabolic): Find a nonzero solution to the singularity equations by the polynomial zero count, then span its semilinear orbit. -> Normalized proper parabolic and radical-order contradiction.
- **step-crossing-growth** [claim](#stmt-grw-towers) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-towers): Iterate crossing degree lower bounds while controlling the lower classical group order. -> Growth beyond every fixed tower after fixed separation.
- **step-crossing-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-grw-no-crossing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-no-crossing): Analyze the final cover category using tower growth, multiplicative quotients, and small-stabilizer parabolics. -> Defining-characteristic preservation on every retained cover.
- **step-common-field** [claim](#stmt-grw-common-field) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-common-field): Use prime coloring with the nonlinear cover's finite field-ratio palette. -> Common endpoint field and family, bounded intermediate ratios, and quadratic growth.
- **step-parabolic-cover-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-grw-no-parabolic-cover) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-no-parabolic-cover): Compare large radical multipliers with multiplicative quotients and bounded-cardinality upper-endpoint multiplier lists. -> No selected cover with a large unipotent radical.
- **step-inner-order-bound** [claim](#stmt-grw-inner-order) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-inner-order): Bound the remaining scalar, inactive, field, and outer multipliers around the nonlinear cover. -> Uniform lower-parameter inner projection order bound.
- **step-remaining-paths** [claim](#stmt-grw-remaining-paths) / [proof](#proof-stmt-grw-remaining-paths): Collect reductions and use fixed-spacing growth to exclude normalization of any proper parabolic. -> Retained paths with nonlinear covers and uniform structural constraints.
- **step-component-preimage** [claim](#stmt-lift-component-preimage) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lift-component-preimage): Lift the normal quasisimple image through a central kernel and identify its perfect derived preimage. -> Characteristic lower component nested in the higher one.
- **step-cohomology-restriction** [claim](#stmt-lift-h1-restriction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lift-h1-restriction): Remove the actual constant section from the induction filtration and exclude maps from restricted simples using height and the equality-case root operators. -> Injective first-cohomology restriction.
- **step-quadratic-form-lift** [claim](#stmt-lift-quadratic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lift-quadratic): Lift the polarization obstruction through first-kernel inflation and injective restriction, then identify the prescribed refinement. -> Preservation of the same form by the rational action.
- **step-nonsingular-line** [claim](#stmt-lift-nonsingular-line) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lift-nonsingular-line): Compute the symmetry kernel, use extension of isometries, and distinguish finite inner points from algebraic vector and line stabilizers. -> Finite symplectic isomorphism and adjoint algebraic vector-stabilizer structure.
- **step-edge-lifts** [claim](#stmt-lift-edge-lifts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lift-edge-lifts): Extract components from retained structures, construct geometric and nonlinear rational maps, and enforce finite compatibility through perfect central covers. -> Nested characteristic components and compatible rational edge maps.
- **step-path-lifts** [claim](#stmt-lift-path-lifts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lift-path-lifts): Compose the chosen finite-compatible edge maps and compare invariant subspaces. -> Pathwise lift and finite-to-algebraic irreducibility implication.
- **step-geometric-irreducibility** [claim](#stmt-lift-geometric-irreducibility) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lift-geometric-irreducibility): Pull irreducibility backwards through the geometric tensor constituent description. -> Irreducible source natural restriction.
- **step-no-parabolic** [claim](#stmt-pkt-no-parabolic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pkt-no-parabolic): Use the fixed-spacing parabolic exclusion already incorporated in the retained chain. -> No comparison stabilizer normalizes a proper parabolic.
- **step-semisimple-section** [claim](#stmt-pkt-semisimple) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pkt-semisimple): Use intrinsic socle and radical flags to force a parabolic unless the characteristic-two nonsingular-line exception occurs. -> Semisimple section with only the stated trivial-factor loss.
- **step-soluble-centralizer** [claim](#stmt-pkt-centralizer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pkt-centralizer): Apply the commuting-normal test to the active component and its centralizer in a proper enlargement. -> Soluble inner centralizer, including the symplectic section.
- **step-multiplicity-bound** [claim](#stmt-pkt-multiplicity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pkt-multiplicity): Describe commuting multiplicity-space isometry groups and construct nonsoluble inner subgroups when multiplicity is too large. -> Absolute constituent multiplicity bound.
- **step-large-packet-bound** [claim](#stmt-pkt-one-packet) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pkt-one-packet): Apply the commuting-normal test to derived groups on disjoint packet unions and then accumulate small packets. -> At most one large packet and bounded remainder dimension.
- **step-field-shifts** [claim](#stmt-pkt-field-shifts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pkt-field-shifts): Compare digit-support shifts on both actual shortcut components and verify support residues for every retained edge category. -> Synchronized field-shift congruence and bounded packet orbit.
- **step-composition-length** [claim](#stmt-pkt-bounded-length) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pkt-bounded-length): Combine absolute multiplicity, packet-size, and dimensional remainder bounds and restore the possible removed factors. -> Uniform absolute natural composition length.
- **step-rank-from-length** [claim](#stmt-irr-rank-length) / [proof](#proof-stmt-irr-rank-length): Apply the corrected high-rank irreducible-triple table and bound diagonal spin block counts by natural composition length. -> Finite ambient-rank palette.
- **step-intervening-rank** [claim](#stmt-irr-intervening) / [proof](#proof-stmt-irr-intervening): Apply the same fixed-representation table to the smallest and intervening groups and compare natural constituent dimensions. -> Exclusion of unbounded diagonal spin ranks.
- **step-stabilized-counts** [claim](#stmt-irr-constituent-count) / [proof](#proof-stmt-irr-constituent-count): Use additivity of trivial and nontrivial counts along restriction and perfectness. -> Irreducibility of every intermediate nontrivial constituent.
- **step-natural-endpoints** [claim](#stmt-irr-natural-endpoints) / [proof](#proof-stmt-irr-natural-endpoints): Ramsey-color factor counts and nonnatural terminal factors; exclude long nonnatural homogeneous triples using the length-based rank palette. -> Arbitrarily long absolutely irreducible natural-endpoint subchains.
- **step-restricted-natural** [claim](#stmt-irr-restricted-natural) / [proof](#proof-stmt-irr-restricted-natural): Use nonnegative restricted highest-weight coefficients and proper invariant subspaces in products of natural or dual modules. -> A single natural or dual-natural factor.
- **step-natural-tail** [claim](#stmt-irr-natural-tail) / [proof](#proof-stmt-irr-natural-tail): Pull irreducibility through a single target composition factor and its natural-type tensor factors. -> Absolute irreducibility of the source natural module.
- **step-chain-rigidity** [claim](#stmt-cls-chain-rigidity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-irr-natural-tail-2): Ramsey-color shortcut terminal factors; exclude the natural alternative by polynomial-versus-iterated growth and the nonnatural alternative by disjoint source-rank intervals. -> Absolute tested-chain rigidity threshold.
- **step-private-insertion** [claim](#stmt-lat-insertion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lat-insertion): Determine cross comparisons and cross lattice operations through the fixed insertion endpoints. -> Finite lattice preserving old operations and exact cover-destruction criterion.
- **step-persistent-fence** [claim](#stmt-lat-persistent-fence) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lat-persistent-fence): Use separate comparability components as complement witnesses and show insertions cannot merge old components. -> Permanent fenced interval.
- **step-shape-batches** [claim](#stmt-lat-shape) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lat-shape): Track designated endpoint pairs to protect covers and exact height-two intervals while inserting fences and coatom witnesses. -> Protected finite chain-test shape with a vertex bound.
- **step-simultaneous-tests** [claim](#stmt-lat-simultaneous) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lat-simultaneous): Separate forward and reverse fresh interiors, freeze target sets, and check all final-batch comparison vertices. -> Simultaneous protected tests, bottlenecks, detector coatoms, and finite size bound.
- **step-decorated-lattice** [claim](#stmt-lat-decorated-lattice) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lat-simultaneous-2): Choose the chain parameter from the absolute threshold, assemble paired horizontal components, and apply rigidity inside the actual forward and reverse filters. -> Finite self-dual decorated lattice with required label equalities and detector data.
- **step-almost-simple-normal** [claim](#stmt-ext-almost-simple) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ext-almost-simple): Compute the centralizer of the inner group and intersect a normal subgroup with it. -> Unique inner socle and trivial soluble radical.
- **step-soluble-fence** [claim](#stmt-ext-soluble-interval) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ext-soluble-interval): Use the nonabelian socle label and quotient an inner-bottom interval by the inner group. -> Exclusion of nontrivial soluble fenced intervals.
- **step-trivial-socle-intersection** [claim](#stmt-ext-trivial-intersection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ext-trivial-intersection): Minimize group order over both orientations; exclude subdirect bottom trace by reversed block intervals and proper product trace by equal-type Boolean vertices. -> Bottom is complementary to the top socle.

- **step-detector-image** [claim](#stmt-ext-detector) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ext-detector): Use the detector coatom property to exclude preserved proper coordinate subgroups, then apply its reverse fence and equal-type multiplicity test. -> Bottom coordinate image contains the full inner group.

  "steps": [
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-frm-normal-test",
      "depends_on": [],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-frm-normal-test",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose that $[D,X]$ is fenced. If $R\\trianglelefteq X$, then either $R\\le D$ or $DR=X$. In particular, $[D,X]$ is not modular. The same assertion applies to a normal subgroup of $X/F$ whenever $F\\trianglelefteq X$ and $F\\le D$, with bottom $D/F$.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-normal-test",
      "inputs": [
        "Fenced interval",
        "Normal subgroup"
      ],
      "method": "Apply the subgroup modular identity to comparable complements and then pass to inverse images in the quotient.",
      "output": "Normal-subgroup dichotomy and nonmodularity.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-frm-normal-test"
    },
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-frm-labels",
      "depends_on": [
        "step-normal-test"
      ],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-frm-labels",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose that $[D,X]$ is fenced, and put $$F_X=\\operatorname{core}_X(D)\n     =\\bigcap_{g\\in X}D^g.$$ Then $X/F_X$ has a unique minimal normal subgroup $$\\label{frm:socle-label}\n S_X=N_X/F_X\\cong T_X^{m_X},$$ where $T_X$ is nonabelian simple and $N_X$ is its full inverse image in $X$. Moreover, $$X=DN_X.$$ Every nontrivial normal subgroup of $X/F_X$ contains $S_X$, and $$C_{X/F_X}(S_X)=1.$$ In particular, $X/F_X$ has no nontrivial soluble normal subgroup. If $I_X$ is the set of simple direct factors of $S_X$, then $D$ and $X$ induce the same transitive permutation group on $I_X$.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-socle-labels",
      "inputs": [
        "Normal-subgroup dichotomy",
        "Supplement correspondence"
      ],
      "method": "Factor out the bottom core; exclude abelian and competing minimal normal subgroups using the fence.",
      "output": "Unique nonabelian socle label and full factor action.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-frm-labels"
    },
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-frm-bottleneck",
      "depends_on": [
        "step-normal-test",
        "step-socle-labels"
      ],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-frm-bottleneck",
          "exact_quote": "Let $D<B\\le Z$, suppose that $[D,B]$ is fenced, and suppose that $B$ is comparable with every member of $[D,Z]$. If $R\\trianglelefteq Z$ and $R\\nleq D$, then $$B=D(R\\cap B).$$ Consequently a soluble normal subgroup of $Z$ is contained in $D$. If $R,Q\\trianglelefteq Z$ and $$[R,Q]\\le F\\trianglelefteq Z,\\qquad F\\le D,$$ then at least one of $R,Q$ is contained in $D$. These conclusions also hold with $B=Z$.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-bottlenecks",
      "inputs": [
        "Labelled bottleneck",
        "Normal subgroups"
      ],
      "method": "Use comparability at the bottleneck and the nonabelian labelled socle.",
      "output": "Soluble-normal and commuting-normal tests above a bottleneck.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-frm-bottleneck"
    },
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-frm-subdirect",
      "depends_on": [],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-frm-subdirect",
          "exact_quote": "Let $T$ be nonabelian simple. Every subdirect subgroup $E\\le T^I$ is a direct product of full diagonal strips on the parts of a partition of $I$. Both the partition and the coordinate identifications within each part are determined by $E$. An inclusion of subdirect subgroups corresponds to a refinement of these parts, with the existing identifications restricted to the smaller parts.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-subdirect-strips",
      "inputs": [
        "Subdirect power"
      ],
      "method": "Induct on coordinates and analyze projection kernels onto a nonabelian simple factor.",
      "output": "Canonical diagonal-strip partition and refinement rule.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-frm-subdirect"
    },
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-frm-equal-transport",
      "depends_on": [
        "step-socle-labels",
        "step-subdirect-strips"
      ],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-frm-equal-transport",
          "exact_quote": "Let $D<X<Y$ be labelled vertices. Then $F_Y\\le F_X$, and $T_X$ is isomorphic to a section of $T_Y$. Put $$E_X=(X\\cap N_Y)/F_Y\\le S_Y.$$ The following conditions are equivalent:*\n\n1.  *$T_X\\cong T_Y$;*\n\n2.  *$E_X$ is subdirect in $S_Y$.*\n\n\n\n*When they hold, the quotient map induces an isomorphism $$\\label{frm:equal-socle-identification}\n E_X\\xrightarrow{\\ \\sim\\ }S_X,\n \\qquad\n N_X=F_X(X\\cap N_Y),\n \\qquad F_X\\cap N_Y=F_Y.$$ Moreover $m_X<m_Y$, and the strip supports give a canonical $X$-equivariant surjection $$\\label{frm:equal-support-map}\n \\sigma_{YX}:I_Y\\longrightarrow I_X.$$ For three comparable labelled vertices of the same simple type these maps compose: $\\sigma_{ZX}=\\sigma_{YX}\\sigma_{ZY}$.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-equal-transport",
      "inputs": [
        "Socle labels",
        "Diagonal strips"
      ],
      "method": "Compare simple sections, use bottom transitivity, and identify subdirect strips with the lower socle.",
      "output": "Equal-type equivalence and composable equivariant support maps.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-frm-equal-transport"
    },
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-frm-strict-product",
      "depends_on": [
        "step-subdirect-strips",

      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-frm-strict-product",
          "exact_quote": "Let $D\\le X<Y$, where $Y$ is labelled. Suppose that the coordinate projections of $$B=(X\\cap N_Y)/F_Y$$ are proper and nontrivial. If $[X,Y]$ is fenced, or if $X$ is a coatom of $[D,Y]$, then $X$ is saturated relative to $Y$.*\n\n*Once $B=P^{I_Y}$ is such a product, no proper subdirect subgroup of $S_Y$ contains $B$. Every coatom of $[X,Y]$, and every intersection of these coatoms, is saturated relative to $Y$. These assertions do not require $X$ to be labelled. For labelled $X<Y$ of different simple types the projection hypothesis holds.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-strict-products",
      "inputs": [
        "Proper nontrivial projections",
        "Diagonal-strip refinement"
      ],
      "method": "Compare the coordinate product closure with comparable fence complements or coatom maximality.",
      "output": "Saturation and saturation of coatom intersections.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-frm-strict-product"
    },
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-frm-projection",
      "depends_on": [
        "step-strict-products"
      ],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-frm-projection",
          "exact_quote": "Let $D\\le X<Y$, with $Y$ labelled, and suppose that $$(X\\cap N_Y)/F_Y=P_X^{I_Y},\\qquad 1<P_X<T_Y.$$ Suppose also that $X$ is an intersection of coatoms of $[X,Y]$; a coatom itself is allowed. Fix $i\\in I_Y$ and let $$\\rho:Y_i\\longrightarrow\\operatorname{Aut}(T_Y)$$ be the action of its factor stabilizer on that coordinate. Identify $T_Y$ with its inner automorphism group, and put $H_* = \\rho(X_i)$. Then $$\\label{frm:inner-bottom}\n H_*\\cap T_Y=P_X.$$ The saturated overgroups of $X$ form a sublattice of $[X,Y]$, and $$\\label{frm:coordinate-interval}\n Z\\longmapsto K_Z=\\rho(Z_i)=H_*P_Z,\n \\qquad (Z\\cap N_Y)/F_Y=P_Z^{I_Y},$$ is an isomorphism from that sublattice onto the entire ordinary subgroup interval $[H_*,H_*T_Y]$. Original covering relations between saturated vertices remain covering relations after projection. In particular, a strict change of simple type at a cover yields a maximal subgroup of an almost simple group, supplementing its simple socle.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-coordinate-projection",
      "inputs": [
        "Saturated bottom",
        "Coatom-intersection representation"
      ],
      "method": "Intersect coatom constraints to identify the inner bottom, then lift all coordinate overgroups.",
      "output": "Entire almost simple coordinate interval preserving covers.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-frm-projection"

    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-frm-active-transport",
      "depends_on": [
        "step-socle-labels",
        "step-coordinate-projection"
      ],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-frm-active-transport",
          "exact_quote": "Let $D<Z\\le Y$ be labelled vertices, and suppose that $Z$ is saturated relative to $Y$: $$(Z\\cap N_Y)/F_Y=P_Z^{I_Y}.$$ Let $K_Z$ be the automorphism group induced by a factor stabilizer in $Z$ on a reference coordinate of $S_Y$. There are $K_Z$-normal subgroups $Q_Z\\le R_Z\\le P_Z$ such that $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\label{frm:product-core}\n (F_Z\\cap N_Y)/F_Y&=Q_Z^{I_Y},\\\\\n \\label{frm:product-active-preimage}\n (N_Z\\cap N_Y)/F_Y&=R_Z^{I_Y},\\\\\n \\label{frm:coordinate-chief}\n R_Z/Q_Z&\\cong T_Z^{a_Z},\\qquad m_Z=a_Zm_Y.\n\\end{aligned}$$ Here $a_Z$ is a positive integer. The section $R_Z/Q_Z$ is a chief factor for the action of $K_Z$ on $P_Z$: there is no $K_Z$-normal subgroup strictly between $Q_Z$ and $R_Z$. Its factors give a $Z$-equivariant surjection $$\\label{frm:product-support}\n \\tau_{ZY}:I_Z\\longrightarrow I_Y$$ whose fibers have size $a_Z$. The stabilizers in $D$ and $Z$ of a coordinate in $I_Y$ induce the same transitive action on its fiber.*\n\n*In addition, suppose $X<Z$ and the hypotheses of Proposition <a href=\"#frm:projection\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"frm:projection\">10</a> hold for $X<Y$. Set $$H_* = \\rho(X_i),\\qquad K_Z=H_*P_Z,\n \\qquad C_Z=\\operatorname{core}_{K_Z}(H_*).$$ Then the subgroups in <a href=\"#frm:product-core\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"frm:product-core\">[frm:product-core]</a> satisfy $$\\label{frm:projected-core}\n Q_Z=C_Z\\cap P_Z,\n \\qquad K_Z=H_*R_Z.$$ Thus $R_ZC_Z/C_Z\\cong R_Z/Q_Z$ is a transitive minimal normal subgroup in the coset action of $K_Z/C_Z$ on $H_*/C_Z$. The groups $H_*$ and $K_Z$ induce the same action on its simple factors. No assertion that this is the entire projected socle is required.*\n\n*If $a_Z=1$, the quotient $P_Z/R_Z$ is soluble.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-active-transport",
      "inputs": [

    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-cls-literature",
      "depends_on": [],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-cls-literature",
          "exact_quote": "The following results are used from the classification and representation theory of finite simple groups.*\n\n1.  *A maximal subgroup of an almost simple classical group, not containing its socle, is a stabilizer in one of Aschbacher’s eight geometric collections, or has an almost simple irreducible component. The geometric collections are subspace or flag stabilizers, direct-sum decompositions, extension-field structures, tensor products, subfield structures, symplectic-type groups, tensor-induced decompositions, and forms. Graph automorphisms may interchange the relevant subspaces or flag members; triality and exceptional graph–field automorphisms occur only in bounded rank. We use (Aschbacher 1984) [[Aschbacher1984](#ref-Aschbacher1984)] and the almost simple formulation and descriptions in (Kleidman and Liebeck 1990, Table 1.2.A and Theorem 1.2.1, pp. 3–4) [[KleidmanLiebeck1990](#ref-KleidmanLiebeck1990)], with the geometric descriptions in Chapters 3–5; the connected tensor structures and their finite fixed-point versions are also given in (Liebeck and Seitz 1998, Theorem 2 and Section 4(5)) [[LiebeckSeitzClassical1998](#ref-LiebeckSeitzClassical1998)].*\n\n2.  *The maximal subgroups of alternating and symmetric groups have the intransitive, imprimitive, affine, diagonal, product-action, or almost simple alternatives of the maximal-subgroup form of the O’Nan–Scott Theorem. The relevant formulation and all the alternatives used here are recorded in the proof of (Burness, Liebeck, and Shalev 2017, Proposition 3.1) [[BurnessLiebeckShalev2017](#ref-BurnessLiebeckShalev2017)].*\n\n3.  *For a fixed algebraic type, sufficiently general finite subgroups lie between the derived group and the inner-diagonal group of a finite fixed-point group. The complementary alternative is containment in a proper algebraic subgroup of bounded complexity. The bounded-envelope version permits passage to the reductive simple quotients of that subgroup; see (Larsen and Pink 2011, Theorems 0.5 and 12.3) [[LarsenPink2011](#ref-LarsenPink2011)].*\n\n4.  *A subgroup maximal in a maximal subgroup of an almost simple group has at most five nonabelian chief factors (Burness, Liebeck, and Shalev 2017, Proposition 8.1) [[BurnessLiebeckShalev2017](#ref-BurnessLiebeckShalev2017)]. The number refers to chief factors, not to their simple direct factors.*\n\n5.  *If $[H,A]$ is a height-two interval and $A$ is alternating or symmetric of degree at least five, it has at most eleven interior vertices (Basile 2001, Theorem D) [[Basile2008](#ref-Basile2008)]. Here the entire interval is required to have height two: $H$ is maximal in every maximal overgroup. This is the hypothesis imposed whenever the result is used.*\n\n6.  *Cross-characteristic irreducible projective degrees satisfy the Landazuri–Seitz lower bounds (Landazuri and Seitz 1974) [[LandazuriSeitz1974](#ref-LandazuriSeitz1974)]. In particular, outside bounded rank, a source of natural dimension $n$ and field parameter $q$ requires degree at least $q^{c n}$ for an absolute $c>0$; the applicable classical bounds are recorded in (Häsä 2014, Tables 3–6) [[Hasa2014](#ref-Hasa2014)]. Above an absolute classical rank, every perfect central cover of a finite simple classical group is a central quotient of its usual simply connected fixed-point group, uniformly over all finite fields, including the standard graph twists (Steinberg 1981, Theorem 1.1 and p. 528) [[Steinberg1981](#ref-Steinberg1981)]. The central-cover deduction and preservation of representations are proved in Lemma <a href=\"#lift:finite-covers\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lift:finite-covers\">44</a>. After passing to that cover, defining-characteristic irreducibles have the Steinberg highest-weight and tensor-product parametrization (Steinberg 1963, Theorems 1.1 and 1.3) [[Steinberg1963](#ref-Steinberg1963)], including the twisted fixed-point groups (Steinberg 1967, Theorem 43) [[SteinbergNotes](#ref-SteinbergNotes)].",
          "source_id": "PM-206.2"
        }
      ],

      "output": "Literature inputs for the uniform reductions.",
      "proof_anchor": "stmt-cls-literature"

Mark its active nonabelian chief factor. There are absolute positive integers $b_0,r_0$ with the following property.*\n\n1.  *The action on the simple factors of the marked chief factor is obtained through at most $r_0$ transitive action levels. Each level either has degree at most $b_0$, or is the natural action of $A_d$ or $S_d$.",

Suppose $$A=H_r\\leq H_{r-1}\\leq\\cdots\\leq H_0=H$$ and every induced action on $H_{j-1}/H_j$ is either of degree at most $b$ or is a natural alternating or symmetric action. There are constants $h,c,k$, depending only on $r,b$, such that:*\n\n1.  *the interval $[A,H]$ has height at most $h$;*\n\n2.  *the set $\\{[H:U]:A\\leq U\\leq H\\}$ has cardinality at most $k$;*\n\n3.  *for every such $U$, its nonabelian composition types belong to $$\\operatorname{cf}_{\\mathrm{na}}(H)\n     \\cup\\{A_{d-j}:A_d\\in\\operatorname{cf}_{\\mathrm{na}}(H),\\ 0\\leq j\\leq c\\}\n     \\cup\\mathcal E_{r,b},$$ where $\\mathcal E_{r,b}$ is a fixed finite set of types.*\n\n*The conclusions also hold for stabilizers of all invariant quotient blocks of the action on $H/A$.",

        {
          "anchor": "stmt-cls-core-gaps",
          "exact_quote": "In the initial projection, consider chain vertices strictly above the original starting vertex $a$, and write $$K_i=H_*P_i,\\qquad C_i=\\operatorname{core}_{K_i}(H_*),\n \\qquad Q_i=C_i\\cap P_i,$$ and let $R_i/Q_i$ be its active nonabelian chief factor. For $i<j$, the inner comparison and its killed kernel are $$J_{ij}=(P_i\\cap R_j)/Q_j,\n \\qquad B_{ij}=(Q_i\\cap R_j)/Q_j.$$ There is an embedding $B_{ij}\\hookrightarrow C_i/C_j$. After deleting at most five nonsoluble gaps, an arbitrarily long subchain remains on which all the $B_{ij}$, including the analogous shortcut kernels, are soluble. There is a constant $c_\\Phi$ such that a finite subgroup $P$ of an algebraic group $X$ of type $\\Phi$ has one of the following descriptions.*\n\n1.  *For a Frobenius map $F_0$, $$E=(X^{F_0})'\\leq P\\leq X^{F_0},$$ where $E$ is simple.*\n\n2.  *Every nonabelian composition factor of $P$ of order greater than $c_\\Phi$ is of Lie type in the characteristic of $X$, with algebraic dimension strictly less than $\\dim X$. The total number of nonabelian composition factors, counted with multiplicity, is at most $c_\\Phi$.*\n\n*In particular, the ranks of nonabelian simple sections of finite groups of Lie type of rank at most $R$ are bounded by a function of $R$; simple sections of bounded order are included in this bound.",

          "exact_quote": "If Theorem <a href=\"#cls:chain-rigidity\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"cls:chain-rigidity\">14</a> is false, then for every $s$ and $R$ there is a retained chain of at least $s$ vertices, with all its original two-edge shortcuts and normal-group tests, such that:*\n\n1.  *all endpoint types are distinct classical types; their ranks, and the ranks of all shortcut middle types, exceed $R$;*\n\n2.  *all endpoint multiplicities are equal. Thus each comparison, projected to one upper active coordinate, has one active simple factor;*\n\n3.  *the killed kernels of all endpoint and shortcut comparisons are soluble. Every endpoint inner comparison has exactly its one active simple factor as a nonabelian composition factor;*\n\n4.  *there is a pool of absolutely bounded cardinality containing all nonabelian simple types in every projected active-factor and fiber stabilizer in the fixed $H_*$, and in their induced images, used in these comparisons. No assertion concerns the entire unprojected original stabilizers. The splitting multiplicities and invariant-block indices have boundedly many possible values;*\n\n5.  *each shortcut is either two strict steps, both with one active simple factor and all other inner composition factors soluble, or a strict split followed downwards by an equal-type merge. The latter is geometric. In geometric steps the inactive dimensions have boundedly many possible values once their simple labels and bounded structural choices are fixed; when all inactive components are soluble these dimensions are absolutely bounded.*\n\n*All bounds described as absolute are uniform over the original groups.           "anchor": "stmt-cls-cat-cross",
          "exact_quote": "<span id=\"cls:catalogue\" label=\"cls:catalogue\"></span> Consider a strict labelled cover and its one-coordinate maximal subgroup $M$ in an almost simple group with socle $T$, as supplied by Proposition <a href=\"#frm:projection\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"frm:projection\">10</a>. There are absolute constants $C,c>0$ with the following properties.*\n\n\n\n1.  *<span id=\"cls:cat-geometric\" label=\"cls:cat-geometric\"></span> For unbounded-rank classical active types, a geometric defining-characteristic step changes natural dimension by taking a subspace or quotient, a repeated natural module, a tensor product, or restriction of scalars. Subfield steps leave natural dimension unchanged and multiply the field exponent by a prime. An extension-field step, read upwards from the active factor, has $$\\label{grw:matrix-field-convention}\n     n_t=b n_s,\\qquad\n     \\epsilon_s f_s=b\\epsilon_t f_t,\n     \\qquad f_t=\\frac{\\epsilon_s}{b\\epsilon_t}f_s,$$ where $b$ is the prime degree between natural matrix fields. A twisted-tensor step has $$\\label{grw:twisted-field-convention}\n     n_t=n_s^b,\\qquad f_s=b f_t,$$ exactly; here $b$ is prime, after bounded source-rank cases are removed. All other changes of field exponent belong to a fixed finite set of positive rational factors.*\n\n2.  *<span id=\"cls:cat-inactive\" label=\"cls:cat-inactive\"></span> If there is one active simple component and the other geometric components are soluble, their natural dimensions are absolutely bounded. The active dimension in a subspace case is comparable with the ambient dimension; a totally singular summand and its dual may represent the same active component twice. A nontrivial parabolic radical in these cases has order between $q^{c n_t}$ and $q^{C n_t^2}$. For a fixed ambient group, once the active slot, other component dimensions, and the bounded flag/form choices are fixed, there are boundedly many possible orders of the full inner stabilizer divided by the order of its active simple factor, with multiplicity included.*\n\n3.  *<span id=\"cls:cat-symplectic\" label=\"cls:cat-symplectic\"></span> A symplectic-type step of unbounded active rank is cross-characteristic. Its source is symplectic or orthogonal over a prime field of order $r$, of natural dimension $2d+O(1)$, and its target natural dimension is $n_t=r^d$. If $P=M\\cap T$, then $$c n_t^2\\leq |P|/|T_s|\\leq C n_t^2.$$ Its target field exponent is at most $|T_s|^C$.*\n\n4.  *<span id=\"cls:cat-nonlinear\" label=\"cls:cat-nonlinear\"></span> After the twisted-tensor case in <a href=\"#cls:cat-geometric\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"cls:cat-geometric\">[cls:cat-geometric]</a> is separated off, a defining-characteristic almost simple irreducible step has a single nonzero restricted, nonnatural Frobenius digit, up to a common Frobenius twist. This restricted module may have further tensor factors in a very special characteristic. Its dimension is at least $c n_s^2$. Its source and target field exponents differ by a rational factor from a fixed finite set. Natural, dual-natural, and natural-size special-isogeny representations are included among the geometric cases instead.*\n\n5.  *For a cross-characteristic almost simple step, $$q_s^{c n_s}\\leq n_t\\leq |T_s|^C,\n     \\qquad f_t\\leq |T_s|^C.$$ The upper degree bound also holds in defining characteristic. For this and the preceding irreducible case, the homomorphism from the ambient automorphism normalizer of the source simple group to its automorphism group has kernel of absolute bounded order. In particular, a subgroup of that normalizer has order at most $C$ times the order of its induced automorphism group of the source.",

The characteristic-two nonsingular-line form inclusion is retained, with its natural simple quotient convention.*\n\n3.  *There are fixed constants $b,C$ and a fixed finite set $\\mathcal R\\subset\\mathbb Q_{>0}$ such that every intermediate exponent satisfies $f'/f\\in\\mathcal R$, every field-extension or twisted-tensor degree is at most $b$, and every inactive geometric natural dimension is at most $b$. In particular each remaining geometric cover satisfies $n_{\\mathrm{target}}\\le C(1+n_{\\mathrm{source}})^b$.*\n\n4.  *There are fixed $c,C>0$ such that $$n_j\\ge c n_i^2,\\qquad |P_{ij}|\\le q^{C n_i^2}.$$ For any prescribed exponent $d$, fixed-spacing thinning gives also $n_j\\ge n_i^d$ for every retained pair, after raising the minimum rank.*\n\n5.  *The coordinate normal tests of Lemma <a href=\"#grw:coordinate-normal-tests\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"grw:coordinate-normal-tests\">[grw:coordinate-normal-tests]</a> remain available for every tested proper coordinate overgroup. <a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-private-lattice-preservation**: A private insertion produces a finite lattice and preserves every meet and join between old vertices.
- **invariant-private-cross-order**: Comparisons between an old vertex and a fresh interior vertex pass through the insertion endpoints.
- **invariant-private-cover-destruction**: An old cover is destroyed exactly when it is the insertion endpoint pair and the inserted lattice has a nonempty interior.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-cover-subdivision**: Insert a nonempty branch directly into a designated shortcut edge while continuing to treat that edge as a cover. -> The fresh interior subdivides the original cover and invalidates the shortcut requirement.
- **anti-nonprivate-comparisons**: Add extra comparisons between old vertices and fresh interior vertices and reuse the preservation guarantee. -> Those additional comparisons fall outside the private insertion definition and may change old meets or joins.
- **anti-local-certificate-as-global-obstruction**: Treat a successful private insertion check as a certificate that the resulting lattice has no finite subgroup-interval representation. -> Preservation of lattice operations does not establish the chain tests, the absolute rigidity threshold, or the extension contradiction.
- **anti-pointwise-transfer**: Infer that a particular lattice checked by the executable has equivalent finite algebra and finite group representation properties. -> The global equivalence transfers the universal representation assertions without asserting pointwise equivalence for an individual lattice.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `constructive`. Private insertion is an explicit finite construction on supplied finite lattices. This executable checks the local lattice, cross-order, preservation, and cover conclusions. It does not certify the absolute chain threshold or either main nonrepresentation theorem.

```python
# INPUTS: JSON containing finite order matrices p and q and endpoint indices a and b.
# PRECONDITIONS: p is a finite lattice; q is a bounded finite lattice with bottom first and top last; a is strictly below b in p.
# OUTPUTS: JSON containing the inserted order matrix and the destroyed old covers; old indices remain unchanged and fresh indices follow them.
# TIME: Finite graph traversals and exhaustive extremum checks; no complexity bound from the paper is asserted.
# SPACE: Finite relation matrices, graph storage, and temporary vertex sets.
# ARITHMETIC: Exact Boolean relations and integer indices.
# FAILURE: Invalid input raises an exception and produces no certificate.
import json
import sys
import networkx as nx


def read_relation(value):
    if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
        raise ValueError('nonempty matrix required')
    n = len(value)
    if any(not isinstance(row, list) or len(row) != n for row in value):
        raise ValueError('square matrix required')
    if any(type(x) not in (int, bool) or x not in (0, 1) for row in value for x in row):
        raise ValueError('Boolean entries required')
    relation = [[bool(x) for x in row] for row in value]
    graph = nx.DiGraph()
    graph.add_nodes_from(range(n))
    graph.add_edges_from((i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j and relation[i][j])
    if not all(relation[i][i] for i in range(n)) or not nx.is_directed_acyclic_graph(graph):
        raise ValueError('partial order required')
    closure = nx.transitive_closure_dag(graph)
    if any(relation[i][j] != (i == j or closure.has_edge(i, j)) for i in range(n) for j in range(n)):
        raise ValueError('transitive matrix required')
    lower = [nx.ancestors(graph, i) | {i} for i in range(n)]
    upper = [nx.descendants(graph, i) | {i} for i in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            common_lower = lower[i] & lower[j]
            common_upper = upper[i] & upper[j]
            maxima = [x for x in common_lower if not any(x != y and relation[x][y] for y in common_lower)]
            minima = [x for x in common_upper if not any(x != y and relation[y][x] for y in common_upper)]
            if len(maxima) != 1 or len(minima) != 1:
                raise ValueError('lattice required')
    return relation


def main():
    payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or set(payload) != {'p', 'q', 'a', 'b'}:
        raise ValueError('input keys')
    p = read_relation(payload['p'])
    q = read_relation(payload['q'])
    a, b = payload['a'], payload['b']
    n, m = len(p), len(q)
    if type(a) is not int or type(b) is not int or not (0 <= a < n and 0 <= b < n):
        raise ValueError('endpoint indices')
    if a == b or not p[a][b]:
        raise ValueError('strict endpoints required')
    if m < 2 or not all(q[0][i] and q[i][m - 1] for i in range(m)):
        raise ValueError('bounded insertion required')
    interior = m - 2
    fresh = list(range(n, n + interior))
    mapping = [a] + fresh + [b]
    graph = nx.DiGraph()
    graph.add_nodes_from(range(n + interior))
    graph.add_edges_from((i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j and p[i][j])
    graph.add_edges_from((mapping[i], mapping[j]) for i in range(m) for j in range(m) if i != j and q[i][j])
    closure = nx.transitive_closure_dag(graph)
    size = n + interior
    order = [[int(i == j or closure.has_edge(i, j)) for j in range(size)] for i in range(size)]
    destroyed = []
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            old_cover = i != j and p[i][j] and not any(k != i and k != j and p[i][k] and p[k][j] for k in range(n))
            if old_cover and (i == a and j == b and interior > 0):
                destroyed.append([i, j])
    print(json.dumps({'order': order, 'destroyed_covers': destroyed}, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

   if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:\n        raise ValueError('nonempty matrix required')\n    n = len(value)\n    if any(not isinstance(row, list) or len(row) != n for row in value):\n        raise ValueError('square matrix required')\n    if any(type(x) not in (int, bool) or x not in (0, 1) for row in value for x in row):\n        raise ValueError('Boolean entries required')\n    relation = [[bool(x) for x in row] for row in value]\n    graph = nx.DiGraph()\n    graph.add_nodes_from(range(n))\n    graph.add_edges_from((i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j and relation[i][j])\n    if not all(relation[i][i] for i in range(n)) or not nx.is_directed_acyclic_graph(graph):\n        raise ValueError('partial order required')\n    closure = nx.transitive_closure_dag(graph)\n    if any(relation[i][j] != (i == j or closure.has_edge(i, j)) for i in range(n) for j in range(n)):\n        raise ValueError('transitive matrix required')\n    lower = [nx.ancestors(graph, i) | {i} for i in range(n)]\n    upper = [nx.descendants(graph, i) | {i} for i in range(n)]\n    for i in range(n):\n        for j in range(n):\n            common_lower = lower[i] & lower[j]\n            common_upper = upper[i] & upper[j]\n            maxima = [x for x in common_lower if not any(x != y and relation[x][y] for y in common_lower)]\n            minima = [x for x in common_upper if not any(x != y and relation[y][x] for y in common_upper)]\n            if len(maxima) != 1 or len(minima) != 1:\n                raise ValueError('lattice required')\n    return relation\n\n\ndef main():\n    payload = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or set(payload) != {'p', 'q', 'a', 'b'}:\n        raise ValueError('input keys')\n    p = read_relation(payload['p'])\n    q = read_relation(payload['q'])\n    a, b = payload['a'], payload['b']\n    n, m = len(p), len(q)\n    if type(a) is not int or type(b) is not int or not (0 <= a < n and 0 <= b < n):\n        raise ValueError('endpoint indices')\n    if a == b or not p[a][b]:\n        raise ValueError('strict endpoints required')\n    if m < 2 or not all(q[0][i] and q[i][m - 1] for i in range(m)):\n        raise ValueError('bounded insertion required')\n    interior = m - 2\n    fresh = list(range(n, n + interior))\n    mapping = [a] + fresh + [b]\n    graph = nx.DiGraph()\n    graph.add_nodes_from(range(n + interior))\n    graph.add_edges_from((i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j and p[i][j])\n    graph.add_edges_from((mapping[i], mapping[j]) for i in range(m) for j in range(m) if i != j and q[i][j])\n    closure = nx.transitive_closure_dag(graph)\n    size = n + interior\n    order = [[int(i == j or closure.has_edge(i, j)) for j in range(size)] for i in range(size)]\n    destroyed = []\n    for i in range(n):\n        for j in range(n):\n            old_cover = i != j and p[i][j] and not any(k != i and k != j and p[i][k] and p[k][j] for k in range(n))\n            if old_cover and (i == a and j == b and interior > 0):\n                destroyed.append([i, j])\n    print(json.dumps({'order': order, 'destroyed_covers': destroyed}, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')))\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",

| software | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | Private insertion supplies a finite operation that a lattice manipulation program can implement while preserving the existing meet and join operations. This contract concerns the insertion operation; producing the final representation obstruction also requires the absolute chain threshold. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The geometric comparisons concern natural modules and finite classical groups. They supply no game state transition, physical evolution, or simulation construction. |

These operations provide a concrete lattice construction, while the parameter needed for the final obstruction is specified through an absolute existence bound. |
| data_structures | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | Private insertion provides a concrete way to extend a finite lattice order while retaining its old meet and join table. The exact cross-order rule constrains how fresh interior vertices attach to the existing structure. |

| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The homomorphism extension dictionary is an algebraic correspondence between invariant subdirect subgroups and extension pairs. No security primitive, adversarial model, or hardness guarantee is constructed. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The natural-module composition-length result bounds algebraic composition factors under subgroup restriction. It supplies no learning procedure, statistical model, or prediction contract. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Minimum group order is used to select a hypothetical representation in a contradiction proof. The paper does not supply an optimization procedure that finds such a representation or certifies an optimum from finite input. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Boolean gluing constructs a homomorphism on generated finite subgroup domains under a common-core hypothesis. It provides no distributed execution, message protocol, or convergence construction. |
| other (Finite lattice theory) | True | strong | adaptable | stated | Private insertion and horizontal summation construct finite lattices while preserving the original Boolean operations. Persistent fences give a source-bound invariant for validating successive insertions. |

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-finite-representing-structures** (formal_scope): The obstruction requires finite representing algebras or finite ambient groups. It does not exclude representations using infinite structures. Blocked use: ['Rejecting an infinite algebra representation because its congruence lattice is finite.', 'Rejecting a countable locally finite group representation.']
- **limit-entire-lattice-versus-embedding** (formal_scope): Realizing the entire congruence lattice is stronger than embedding a finite lattice into a partition lattice. Blocked use: ['Using the negative theorem to reject a meet- and join-preserving partition-lattice embedding.']
- **limit-global-transfer-only** (formal_scope): The representation equivalence transfers universal assertions. The constructed subgroup-interval obstruction is not identified pointwise with the existential congruence-lattice obstruction. Blocked use: ['Claiming that the same prescribed lattice has equivalent finite algebra and finite group representation properties.']
- **limit-existence-not-decision** (unknown): A general decision procedure for representability from an arbitrary finite order table is ABSENT. The paper addresses the existence of an obstruction. <a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We give a negative solution to the finite lattice representation problem. We prove that there is a finite nonempty lattice that is not the full congruence lattice of any finite nonempty algebra of any finite signature.

<a id="pm-h-1"></a>
#### Statements index
